name: Leucite
chronometers: ⁴⁰Ar/³⁹Ar (K-rich volcanic rocks); crystal size distributions
setting: rendered in the cubic Ia3̄d pseudo-cell (true room-T cell I4₁/a)

matrix.title: Icositetrahedron with cube and dodecahedron
matrix.subtitle: Leucite grows as cubic leucite and on cooling inverts to twinned tetragonal domains that keep the cubic {211} shape. The matrix is a truncation series around that icositetrahedron.
matrix.note: Rendered with cubic symmetry because twinned natural crystals keep the cubic external shape. Using the true tetragonal room-temperature cell would split {211} into three forms whose angles differ by up to 0.8°. Groundmass leucite is often rounded.

about: Leucite is the classic example of a paramorph: it crystallizes as cubic leucite above about 600–690 °C, then inverts to finely twinned tetragonal domains while keeping its 24-faced icositetrahedral {211} shape. Leucite textures and size distributions record magmatic processes before eruptions (Shea et al. 2009).

references.note: The cubic–tetragonal transition behind the pseudocubic twinning.

references.citation: Shea, T., Larsen, J.F., Gurioli, L., Hammer, J.E., Houghton, B.F., Cioni, R. (2009). Leucite crystals: surviving witnesses of magmatic processes preceding the 79AD eruption at Vesuvius, Italy. Earth and Planetary Science Letters 281, 88–98.
references.note: Leucite textures and crystal size distributions as records of magmatic timescales.
